title: Kfb: knit front and back
subtitle: A simple one-stitch increase that leaves a small bar.
excerpt: Kfb (knit front and back) works one stitch twice, producing two stitches from one. The easiest visible increase, with a characteristic horizontal bar on the left stitch.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), increases chapter. Weldon's Practical Knitter (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: Knit front and back: an increase worked by knitting into the front of a stitch and then into the back of the same stitch before slipping it off the needle. Produces two stitches from one, with a visible horizontal bar on the left new stitch.

content.text: Kfb (also written k1f&b, or 'knit into the front and back') is the most straightforward visible increase in plain knitting. You knit into the front of a stitch as normal but do not drop it; then you swing the right needle to the back of the same stitch and knit into the back loop, before finally slipping the stitch off. The result is
, with a small horizontal bar visible on the left stitch. Difficulty: beginner.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows worked
Insert the right needle into the front of the stitch as if to knit. Wrap the yarn and draw the loop through, but do not drop the stitch from the left needle.
Rotate the right needle to the back of the same stitch. Insert the tip into the back loop of the same stitch.
Wrap the yarn and draw a second loop through.
Slip the original stitch off the left needle. Two new stitches are on the right needle.

Kfb is used in garter-stitch shawls and triangular scarves where the visible bar serves as a decorative element on each increase row. It appears in some hat patterns for the body shaping and in traditional sock toe constructions. Where the bar is undesirable, M1L and M1R are preferred; where simplicity is more important than invisibility, kfb is the right choice.

items.symptom: Stitch dropped before the second entry
items.cause: Releasing the stitch from the left needle at step 1
items.fix: Consciously keep the original stitch on the left needle after the first wrap. It should feel slightly awkward until the motion becomes automatic.

items.symptom: Cannot find the back of the stitch for step 2
items.cause: The right needle needs to enter from the right side of the left needle
items.fix: After step 1, rotate the right needle clockwise so its tip points toward the back of the work. The back leg of the stitch will be clearly visible.

items.symptom: Bar is very visible and distracting
items.cause: Normal result of the kfb method
items.fix: If an invisible increase is needed, use M1L or M1R instead. The bar in kfb is a structural feature, not a fault.
